53001.text: In a given configuration, how should the aircraft be loaded for the stall speed to be highest?
options: with maximum permitted mass and the CG furthest forward.
with low total mass and the CG furthest aft.
with low total mass and the CG furthest forward.
with maximum permitted mass and the CG furthest aft.
with maximum permitted mass and the CG outside the limits.

53002.text: Which of the following causes the position of the centre of gravity (CG) to shift within the limits?

53003.text: Which of the following is equal to the distance of the centre of gravity from the datum?

53004.text: If the stall speed of the aircraft in the landing configuration is 50 knots, what will the Vref value be?

53005.text: How will a higher aircraft mass affect the rotation speed and the take-off safety speed?
options: The rotation speed will increase and the take-off safety speed will decrease.
The rotation speed will decrease and the take-off safety speed will increase.
The take-off distance will also increase.

53006.text: Which performance variable is independent of runway slope?

53007.text: Wing contamination caused by a small amount of ice accumulating on the wing:
options: produces more drag, more weight and less lift.
causes an increase in weight and a decrease in drag.
reduces both the lift and drag coefficients.
increases both the lift and drag coefficients.
increases the stall speed by disturbing the airflow over the wing.

53008.text: Which of the following is not a factor affecting the landing distance?
options: Runway slope and the hydroplaning (water cushion) effect
The effect of landing mass and landing speed
is the distance between brake release and the aircraft reaching VLOF speed.
is the distance between brake release and the aircraft becoming airborne.
is the distance between brake release and the start of the climb.
is the distance between brake release and the aircraft lifting off the runway and climbing to 400 ft.
is the distance between brake release and the aircraft lifting off the runway and climbing to 50 ft.

53010.text: What is the average rate of climb of an aircraft that can climb 5500 feet in 12 minutes?

53011.text: Which of the following shows how a cruising speed of 90 knots is entered in the relevant field of the ICAO flight plan?

53012.text: If an aircraft can fly 189 NM in 30 minutes in still air, how far can it fly in 30 minutes in a 30 kt headwind?

53013.text: What is the mass in kg of 50 litres of fuel with a specific gravity of 0.72?

53014.text: An aircraft is flying between A and B. The distance between the two points is 600 NM. The fuel consumption is 10 US gallons per hour. If the aircraft has 90 US gal of fuel in total and the ground speed (GS) is 200 knots, how much fuel will remain?

53015.text: How many kilograms is 151 litres of AVGAS? (Specific gravity 0.72)

53016.text: What is the relationship between US-GAL and litres?

53017.text: If 15 litres of fuel are consumed in 34 minutes, what is the fuel consumption rate?

53018.text: What is the maximum time an aircraft with a fuel consumption of 25 gal/hour can remain airborne with 80 gallons of fuel?

53019.text: If an aircraft with a fuel capacity of 72 gallons has a fuel consumption of 15 gal/hour, what is the maximum endurance?

53020.text: Which of the following correctly defines the useful load?
options: The sum of usable fuel and traffic load.
The difference between take-off mass and usable fuel.
The difference between take-off mass and traffic load.
The difference between maximum take-off mass and empty mass.
